newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU chemical industry favours single currency.
newsitem.headline: EU chemical industry favours single currency.

text.p: Europe's chemical industry threw its weight firmly behind the European Union's planned single currency on Friday, saying the euro would help boost growth as well as investment conditions on the continent.
The European Chemical Industry Council (CEFIC) said it welcomed the introduction of a single and strong currency.
"The end of exchange rate fluctuations and distortions will allow companies to plan more reliably. The costs of foreign exchange management will be saved," said CEFIC president Jurgen Dormann.
Dormann, speaking at CEFIC's general assembly in Geneva, said the major benefit expected from economic and monetary union (EMU) was competitiveness and growth.

"CEFIC considers monetary union the necessary step to complete the full economic integration of Europe; it therefore welcomes the introduction of a single and strong currency," he said, according to a statement issued in Brussels.
Chemical companies were preparing for the conversion to the euro, he said.
CEFIC also said it hoped that as many countries as possible would be able to take part in EMU from the start.
